Top-p keeps the smallest set whose cumulative probability ≥ p, so it adapts to the model's confidence. After filtering, probabilities are renormalised and a token is sampled.

q: Greedy vs beam search vs sampling?
a: Greedy picks the top token each step: fast but can loop. Beam search tracks the B best sequences: good for translation/summarisation, bland for chat. Sampling with temperature/top-p gives diverse, natural text for open-ended generation.

q: What settings would you use for a RAG answer vs brainstorming?
a: RAG, extraction, SQL: temperature 0–0.2, structured output, citations. Brainstorming or creative writing: temperature ~0.9–1.2 with top-p ~0.9–0.95.

q: How do you force an LLM to output valid JSON?
a: Use the provider's structured output / JSON schema mode or function calling, which constrains decoding to valid tokens; or grammar-constrained decoding for open models. Validate with Pydantic and retry with the error message if parsing fails.

Why is top-p often preferred over top-k?
a: Top-p adapts to the model's confidence: when one token has 95% probability it keeps just that one; when the distribution is flat it keeps many. A fixed top-k keeps the same number of candidates in both cases, allowing junk when confident and cutting off good options when uncertain.

q: How does speculative decoding speed things up without changing quality?
a: A small draft model proposes several tokens; the large model scores all of them in one forward pass and accepts the longest prefix consistent with its own distribution (with a correction step). Several tokens per large-model pass, mathematically the same output distribution.

Time to first token (driven by prefill and prompt length) and time per output token (driven by decode speed). Users feel TTFT most, so shorter prompts, prompt caching and streaming help perceived latency.

q: Ways to make LLM inference faster?
a: KV cache, quantisation (INT8/4-bit), continuous batching and PagedAttention (vLLM), speculative decoding, FlashAttention, prompt caching, smaller or distilled models, and shorter prompts/outputs.
